definition_en: the whole physical structure of a person or animal
core_image: 镜前伸展四肢的人
scene: 清晨他站在镜子前活动身体。He stretched his whole body before running.
sceneCN: 这里 body 是「身体」（第 1 个义项：人或动物的整个躯体）；句意是跑步前他伸展了整个身体。

senses.title: The physical form of a person
senses.definition: the whole physical structure of a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物完整的躯体结构
senses.example: He stretched his whole body before running.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步前他伸展了整个身体。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming the trunk and then the whole living form.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，先指躯干，后指整个活着的躯体。

senses.title: A dead person
senses.definition: the dead body of a person
senses.definitionCN: 人死后的躯体
senses.example: The police found a body in the river.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在河里发现了一具尸体。
senses.why: A corpse is still a body, so the same word serves for the dead.
senses.whyCN: 尸体仍然是一具躯体，所以同一个词也用来指死者。

senses.title: The main part
senses.definition: the main or central part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物最主要或居中的部分
senses.example: The body of the report is only ten pages.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的主体只有十页。
senses.why: A trunk is the main part of a tree, and the word spread to texts and groups.
senses.whyCN: 树干是树的主体，这个词便扩展到文本与团体。

intro.en: Body is an Old English word for the trunk, later widened to the whole person.
intro.cn: body 是古英语中指躯干的词，后来扩展到整个人。

items.en: body of water and body of law named main wholes.
items.cn: body of water 与 body of law 用来指一个整体。

items.cn: 如今 body 兼指躯体、尸体与主体。

note.cn: 形近组共有 b-o-d 的字母形状；近义组指身形与尸体。

normal.en: A bodyguard protects a person.

normal.en: Bodily means related to the body.
normal.cn: bodily 意为与身体有关的。

definition_zh: 沸腾；煮沸；煮（食物）；非常愤怒
definition_en: to heat a liquid until it bubbles
core_image: 锅底不断冒起的水泡
scene: 锅里的水过了几分钟开始翻滚。The water began to boil after a few minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 boil 是「沸腾」（第 1 个义项：液体受热冒出气泡）；句意是几分钟后水开始沸腾。

senses.title: To bubble with heat
senses.definition: to heat a liquid until it bubbles and gives off steam
senses.definitionCN: 把液体加热到冒泡并冒出蒸汽
senses.example: The water began to boil after a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 几分钟后水开始沸腾。
senses.why: This is the core sense, taken from the Latin word for a bubble.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自拉丁语中表示气泡的词。

senses.title: To cook in hot water
senses.definition: to cook food in water that is boiling
senses.definitionCN: 在沸腾的水中烹煮食物
senses.example: She boiled two eggs for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她早饭煮了两个鸡蛋。
senses.why: Cooking in bubbling water is the everyday use of the same action.
senses.whyCN: 在冒泡的水里烹煮，是这一动作最常见的用法。

senses.title: To be very angry
senses.definition: to feel extremely angry, as if heat were rising
senses.definitionCN: 极度愤怒，像热气往上冲
senses.example: He was boiling with anger after the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会后他怒火中烧。
senses.why: Anger is pictured as heat, so the bubbling of water became a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被比作高温，水的翻滚便引申为情绪。

intro.en: Boil goes back through French to Latin bulla, a bubble.
intro.cn: boil 经法语上溯到拉丁语 bulla，意思是气泡。

items.en: bulla meant a bubble or a round object.
items.cn: bulla 指气泡或圆形之物。

items.en: boillir meant to bubble and to cook in water.
items.cn: boillir 指冒泡，也指用水煮。

items.en: boilen covered both water and cooking.
items.cn: boilen 同时指水的沸腾与烹煮。

items.en: boil over described liquid running over the pot.
items.cn: boil over 指液体沸出锅外。

items.en: boil also describes violent anger.
items.cn: 如今 boil 也可形容暴怒。

note.en: The look-alike group rhymes with boil; the near-meaning group names other ways of heating food.
note.cn: 形近组与 boil 押韵；近义组是其他加热食物的方式。

abstract.en: See steam clouding a kitchen window.

sensesIntro.en: A liquid bubbling, food cooking in it, and anger that feels like heat.

definition_en: brave and confident enough to take risks
core_image: 会议室里第一个站起来发言的人
scene: 他在会上第一个站起来反对。It was a bold move to speak first at the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 bold 是「大胆的」（第 1 个义项：敢于冒险、不怕后果）；句意是在会上第一个发言是个大胆的举动。

pos.zh: 形容词：大胆的；粗体的；鲜明的

senses.title: Brave and confident
senses.definition: willing to take risks and say what you think
senses.definitionCN: 愿意冒险并敢于说出自己的想法
senses.example: It was a bold move to speak first at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 在会上第一个发言是个大胆的举动。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming a person who is not afraid.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指无所畏惧的人。

senses.title: Thick and dark in print
senses.definition: printed with thick dark lines that stand out
senses.definitionCN: 用又粗又深的线条印出，显得突出
senses.example: The title is printed in bold type.
senses.exampleCN: 标题用粗体印刷。
senses.why: A bold person stands out, and thick letters were seen the same way.
senses.whyCN: 大胆的人很显眼，粗重的字母也同样显眼。

senses.title: Strong and easy to see
senses.definition: strong and clear in colour or shape
senses.definitionCN: 颜色或形状强烈而清晰
senses.example: She painted the wall in bold colours.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了鲜明的颜色。
senses.why: Anything that forces the eye to stop was called bold.
senses.whyCN: 任何能抓住目光的东西都被称为 bold。

intro.en: Bold is an Old English word for a brave man.

items.en: bald meant bold and fearless.

items.en: bold kept the sense of courage in battle.

items.en: bold type named thick letters that stand out.

items.en: bold colours described strong, clear shades.

definition_zh: 螺栓；门闩；猛冲；一道闪电
definition_en: a metal bar that slides across to lock a door
core_image: 夜里插紧的门闩
scene: 睡前她把门闩插好。She bolted the door before going to bed.
sceneCN: 这里 bolt 是「门闩；插上闩」（第 2 个义项：门上滑动的锁）；句意是睡前她把门闩好。

senses.title: A metal fastener
senses.definition: a thick metal pin used to hold parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把部件固定在一起的粗金属销
senses.example: The mechanic tightened every bolt on the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工把车轮上的每颗螺栓都拧紧了。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming the metal pin that shoots through a hole.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指穿过孔洞的金属销。

senses.title: A bar that locks a door
senses.definition: a sliding bar that keeps a door closed
senses.definitionCN: 让门保持关闭的滑动横杆
senses.example: She bolted the door before going to bed.
senses.exampleCN: 睡前她把门闩好。
senses.why: A door bar works like a bolt shot into place.
senses.whyCN: 门上的横杆就像射入锁孔的螺栓。

senses.title: To run away suddenly
senses.definition: to move or run away very suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然快速移动或逃走
senses.example: The horse bolted when it heard the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 马听到响声就惊跑了。
senses.why: Something that bolts leaves like a bolt shot from a gun.
senses.whyCN: bolt 的离开就像子弹被射出一样。

senses.title: A flash of lightning
senses.definition: a sudden flash of lightning
senses.definitionCN: 突然划过的闪电
senses.example: A bolt of lightning lit the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 一道闪电照亮了天空。
senses.why: Lightning looks like a metal shaft thrown across the sky.
senses.whyCN: 闪电看起来像一支金属箭划过天空。

items.en: bolt covers fastening, locking, running and lightning.

note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组分别是锁具与奔跑。

abstract.cn: 想象一支粗箭射进墙里。

abstract.en: See a white flash splitting the sky.

definition_en: a device that explodes and causes damage
core_image: 桥下被围起来的黑色装置
scene: 拆弹手小心地靠近桥下的那枚装置。The bomb was found under the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 bomb 是「炸弹」（第 1 个义项：会爆炸并造成破坏的装置）；句意是桥下发现了一枚炸弹。

senses.title: An explosive device
senses.definition: a device that explodes and causes damage
senses.definitionCN: 会爆炸并造成破坏的装置
senses.example: The bomb was found under the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 桥下发现了一枚炸弹。
senses.why: This is the core sense, from a word for a booming sound.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自表示轰响的词。

senses.title: To attack with bombs
senses.definition: to attack a place by dropping bombs on it
senses.definitionCN: 向某地投掷炸弹进行攻击
senses.example: Enemy planes bombed the port at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 敌机在黎明时轰炸了港口。
senses.why: The noun became a verb as soon as bombs were used in war.
senses.whyCN: 炸弹一用于战争，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: To fail badly
senses.definition: to fail completely, as a play or a film might
senses.definitionCN: 彻底失败，如戏剧或电影票房惨淡
senses.example: The new play bombed with critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这出新戏被评论界批得很惨。
senses.why: A failure that goes down like an explosion kept the image of the bomb.
senses.whyCN: 像爆炸一样轰然倒下的失败，沿用炸弹的意象。

items.en: bombus meant a deep booming sound.

items.en: bombe named an exploding shell.

items.en: bomb entered English as a word for a shell.
items.cn: bomb 以炮弹之义进入英语。

items.en: bombing from aircraft made the verb common.
items.cn: 飞机投弹使动词用法普及。

items.en: bomb also means to fail badly in slang.

a substance that can blow things apart
a small bomb thrown by hand

normal.en: Bomb and bombard share the same base.

normal.cn: 定时炸弹在设定时刻爆炸。

normal.en: The verb bomb means to attack from the air.

normal.en: A bomber is an aircraft or a person.

normal.en: A bomb scare empties a building.

abstract.en: See a dark object roped off on a bridge.

abstract.en: See a flash and a cloud of dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闪光与一团尘土。

abstract.en: See an empty theatre after a bad play.
abstract.cn: 想象一出烂戏之后空荡的剧场。

examples.en: The bomb was found under the bridge.

examples.en: Enemy planes bombed the port at dawn.

definition_en: a strong connection between people
core_image: 两个孩子牵着同一根绳子
scene: 两个孩子一起长大，之间有一种牢固的联结。A strong bond grew between the two children.
sceneCN: 这里 bond 是「纽带；联系」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间的情感连接）；句意是两个孩子之间形成了牢固的纽带。

senses.title: A close connection
senses.definition: a strong feeling that connects people
senses.definitionCN: 把人们连在一起的情感
senses.example: A strong bond grew between the two children.
senses.exampleCN: 两个孩子之间形成了牢固的纽带。
senses.why: This comes from the oldest sense of something that ties.
senses.whyCN: 这来自「系住」的最古老含义。

senses.title: A financial certificate
senses.definition: a document promising to repay money with interest
senses.definitionCN: 承诺连本带息偿还的凭证
senses.example: He bought a government bond for his savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他把积蓄买了政府债券。
senses.why: A bond ties the lender and the borrower until the money is repaid.
senses.whyCN: 债券把出借人与借款人系在一起，直到还清为止。

senses.title: To join firmly
senses.definition: to stick things together very strongly
senses.definitionCN: 把物体牢牢粘合在一起
senses.example: The glue bonds wood to metal.
senses.exampleCN: 这种胶能把木头粘到金属上。
senses.why: The verb keeps the physical image of tying two things into one.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了把两物系成一体的具体意象。

intro.en: Bond comes from an Old Norse word for something that ties.
intro.cn: bond 来自古诺尔斯语中表示「系住之物」的词。

items.en: band meant a thing that ties or binds.
items.cn: band 指用来系或捆的东西。

items.en: bond named a rope, a chain and a duty.
items.cn: bond 指绳索、锁链，也指义务。

items.en: a bond became a written promise to pay.
items.cn: bond 成为一种书面的付款承诺。

items.en: chemists spoke of the bond between atoms.
items.cn: 化学家开始用 bond 指原子之间的键。

items.en: bond covers feelings, money and glue.
items.cn: 如今 bond 兼指情感、债券与黏合。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group names ties and links.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是表示联系与连接的词。

entries.definition: a thin strip that holds things
a relationship between people or things

normalIntro.en: Bond is a rope you cannot see: it holds people, money and atoms.
normalIntro.cn: bond 是一根看不见的绳：系住人、金钱与原子。

normal.en: Bond and bonds are singular and plural.
normal.cn: 单数是 bond，复数是 bonds。

normal.en: A family bond holds people together.
normal.cn: 家庭纽带把人们连在一起。

normal.en: A government bond is a loan to the state.
normal.cn: 政府债券是借给国家的钱。

normal.en: Glue bonds two surfaces.
normal.cn: 胶水把两个表面粘住。

normal.en: Bondage means being tied or trapped.
normal.cn: bondage 意为被束缚或奴役。

abstract.en: See two children holding one rope.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子牵着同一根绳。

abstract.en: See a paper certificate locked in a safe.
abstract.cn: 想象一张锁在保险箱里的凭证。

abstract.en: See two boards pressed together by glue.
abstract.cn: 想象两块木板被胶压在一起。

examples.en: A strong bond grew between the two children.
examples.cn: 两个孩子之间形成了牢固的纽带。

examples.en: He bought a government bond for his savings.
examples.cn: 他把积蓄买了政府债券。

examples.en: The glue bonds wood to metal.
examples.cn: 这种胶能把木头粘到金属上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 bond 想成「绑的」：绑在一起就是联系，借据把人绑住就是债券。

root: bond 源自古诺尔斯语 band，本指用来系捆的东西，中古英语指绳索、锁链与义务，后来发展出债券、化学键与情感纽带等义。

sensesIntro.en: A tie between people, a paper promise to pay, and the act of joining.
sensesIntro.cn: 人与人之间的连接、书面的还款承诺，以及结合的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two children holding the same rope.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个孩子牵着同一根绳子。

intro.en: Bond takes -age and -holder to name a state and a person.
intro.cn: bond 加 -age 与 -holder 可表示状态与持有者。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old Norse; the items below share the idea of tying.

definition_en: one of the hard parts inside the body of a person or animal
core_image: 灯光下泛白的骨头
scene: 医生指着片子上的那处阴影。The scan showed a small crack in the bone.
sceneCN: 这里 bone 是「骨头」（第 1 个义项：人或动物体内的硬组织）；句意是片子显示骨头上有一道小裂痕。

senses.title: A hard part of the skeleton
senses.definition: one of the hard parts that form the skeleton
senses.definitionCN: 构成骨架的坚硬部分之一
senses.example: The scan showed a small crack in the bone.
senses.exampleCN: 片子显示骨头上有一道小裂痕。
senses.why: This is the oldest and central sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老、最核心的义项。

senses.title: The skeleton as a whole
senses.definition: the whole set of bones in a body
senses.definitionCN: 体内全部骨头的总称
senses.example: The old horse was nothing but skin and bone.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹老马瘦得只剩皮包骨。
senses.why: A single bone stands for the whole frame it belongs to.
senses.whyCN: 一根骨头可以代表它所属的整个骨架。

senses.title: To remove the bones
senses.definition: to take the bones out of meat or fish
senses.definitionCN: 把肉或鱼中的骨头去掉
senses.example: The chef boned the fish before cooking it.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师在烹煮前把鱼骨去掉。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb meaning to take its bones away.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，表示把骨头取走。

intro.en: Bone is an Old English word that has kept its meaning for a thousand years.
intro.cn: bone 是古英语词，一千年来意思几乎没变。

items.en: ban meant a bone of the body.
items.cn: ban 指身体中的骨头。

items.en: bone named the frame of the body.
items.cn: bone 指身体的骨架。

items.en: a bone to pick meant a matter to argue about.
items.cn: a bone to pick 指可争辩的事。

items.en: to bone meat became a kitchen verb.
items.cn: 去骨成为厨房里的动词。

items.en: bone covers a single bone and the whole skeleton.
items.cn: 如今 bone 兼指一根骨头与整个骨骼。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names parts of the skeleton.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是骨骼的组成部分。

entries.definition: all the bones of a body

normalIntro.en: Bone is the white frame inside every body.
normalIntro.cn: bone 是每具身体里那副白色的支架。

normal.en: Bone and bones are singular and plural.
normal.cn: 单数是 bone，复数是 bones。

normal.en: Bone marrow is inside large bones.
normal.cn: 骨髓长在大骨头的里面。

normal.en: Bony means very thin.
normal.cn: bony 意为瘦骨嶙峋的。

normal.en: A backbone supports the spine.
normal.cn: backbone 支撑脊柱。

normal.en: To bone a fish is to remove its bones.
normal.cn: 给鱼去骨就是把鱼刺取出。

abstract.en: See a white bone under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下泛白的一根骨头。

abstract.en: See a whole skeleton in a museum.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆里的一整副骨架。

abstract.en: See a cook lifting bones from a fish.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师把鱼骨挑出来。

examples.en: The scan showed a small crack in the bone.
examples.cn: 片子显示骨头上有一道小裂痕。

examples.en: She broke a bone in her foot.
examples.cn: 她脚上的一块骨头骨折了。

examples.en: The chef boned the fish before cooking it.
examples.cn: 厨师在烹煮前把鱼骨去掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: bone 读起来像「棒」：骨头硬得像一根小棒，一根根撑起身体。

root: bone 源自古英语 ban，本指身体中的骨头，中古英语起可指整个骨架，后来又产生「去骨」的动词用法。

sensesIntro.en: One hard part of the skeleton, the whole skeleton, and the act of removing bones.
sensesIntro.cn: 骨架中的一块硬骨、整个骨骼，以及去骨的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white bone under a lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯光下泛白的一根骨头。

intro.en: Bone takes -y and -less, and joins backbone as a compound.

all the bones of a body

definition_en: extra money paid to an employee as a reward
core_image: 年底发到手里的额外信封
scene: 年终公司给每个人发了一笔奖金。Everyone received a bonus at the end of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 bonus 是「奖金」（第 1 个义项：工资之外的额外报酬）；句意是年底每个人都拿到一笔奖金。

derivatives.zh: 语义关联词，义为奖金、赏金

senses.title: Extra pay for work
senses.definition: extra money added to normal pay as a reward
senses.definitionCN: 在正常工资之外额外支付的报酬
senses.example: Everyone received a bonus at the end of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 年底每个人都拿到一笔奖金。
senses.why: This is the main sense, from the Latin word for good.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要义项，来自拉丁语中表示「好」的词。

senses.title: Something extra and good
senses.definition: an unexpected advantage that comes with something
senses.definitionCN: 随某事物而来的意外好处
senses.example: Free breakfast was an added bonus.
senses.exampleCN: 免费早餐是个额外的好处。
senses.why: Anything good beyond what was promised is felt as a bonus.
senses.whyCN: 超出承诺的任何好事，都会被当成一份额外奖励。

intro.en: Bonus is Latin for good, and it entered English through the stock market.
intro.cn: bonus 在拉丁语中意为「好的」，经股票市场进入英语。

items.en: bonus meant good or honest.
items.cn: bonus 意为好的、诚实的。

items.en: London brokers called a extra payment a bonus.
items.cn: 伦敦经纪人把额外的付款称为 bonus。

items.en: bonus named a share of profit paid to workers.
items.cn: bonus 指发给工人的一份利润。

items.en: bonus spread to any extra benefit.
items.cn: bonus 扩展到任何额外的好处。

items.en: bonus means extra pay or an added advantage.
items.cn: 如今 bonus 指奖金或额外的好处。

note.en: The look-alike group starts with bon-; the near-meaning group names rewards and perks.
note.cn: 形近组都以 bon- 开头；近义组是奖励与福利。

normal.en: A bonus point is extra credit.

normal.en: Bonanza means a sudden lucky gain.

abstract.en: See an extra envelope at the end of December.

sensesIntro.en: Extra money for work, and any good thing added on.

definition_en: a set of printed pages fastened together inside a cover
core_image: 窗边翻开的旧书
scene: 她在窗边翻着一本旧书。She was reading an old book by the window.

senses.title: Printed pages bound together

senses.definitionCN: 装订在封面内的一叠印刷书页
senses.example: She was reading an old book by the window.

items.cn: 如今 bother 兼指打扰、费心与麻烦。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by letters; the near-meaning group names disturbing and annoying.
note.cn: 形近组字母相近；近义组是打扰与使人生气。

normalIntro.en: Bother is a small knock at a bad time, and the effort you would rather not make.
normalIntro.cn: bother 是不合时宜的一声敲门，也是你不愿花的那份力气。

normal.en: Bother and bothered are the base and past forms.
normal.cn: 原形是 bother，过去式是 bothered。

normal.en: Sorry to bother you is a polite opening.
normal.cn: sorry to bother you 是礼貌的开场。

normal.en: Don't bother means no effort is needed.
normal.cn: don't bother 意为不必费心。

normal.en: A bothersome fly will not leave.
normal.cn: 恼人的苍蝇赶不走。

normal.en: A bit of bother means a small problem.
normal.cn: a bit of bother 指一点小麻烦。

abstract.en: See a hand hesitating before a door.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在门前犹豫。

abstract.en: See someone waving away an offer of help.
abstract.cn: 想象有人摆手谢绝帮忙。

abstract.en: See a fly circling a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一只苍蝇绕着灯打转。

examples.en: He knocked softly so as not to bother anyone.
examples.cn: 他轻轻敲门，以免打扰别人。

examples.en: Don't bother cooking for me.
examples.cn: 不用为我费心做饭了。

examples.en: The delay was a bit of a bother.
examples.cn: 这次延误有点麻烦。

dict_mnemonic.text: bo 像「拨」，ther 像「人」：总去拨弄别人，就是打扰；自己懒得拨，就是不想费心。

root: bother 十八世纪才出现在英语中，来源不明，最初表示使人困惑或担忧，后来兼指打扰、费心与麻烦事。

sensesIntro.en: Interrupting someone, taking the trouble, and the trouble itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 打断别人、不嫌麻烦地去做，以及麻烦本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft knock at a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：门上轻轻的一敲。

intro.en: Bother takes -some and -ation to make an adjective and a noun.
intro.cn: bother 加 -some 与 -ation 可构成形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is of uncertain origin; the items below are related in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来源不明，下面的词只在意思上相关。

definition_en: a glass or plastic container with a narrow neck for liquid
core_image: 桌上立着的空玻璃瓶
scene: 桌上放着一只空玻璃瓶。An empty glass bottle stood on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 bottle 是「瓶子」（第 1 个义项：细颈的液体容器）；句意是桌上放着一只空玻璃瓶。

senses.title: A container for liquid
senses.definition: a glass or plastic container with a narrow neck
senses.definitionCN: 有细颈的玻璃或塑料容器
senses.example: An empty glass bottle stood on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上放着一只空玻璃瓶。
senses.why: This is the core sense, from a word for a cask.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，来自表示木桶的词。

senses.title: The amount inside
senses.definition: the amount of liquid that a bottle holds
senses.definitionCN: 一个瓶子所能装下的液量
senses.example: He drank a whole bottle of water.
senses.exampleCN: 他喝了一整瓶水。
senses.why: A container often stands for the amount it carries.
senses.whyCN: 容器常被用来代指它所装的量。

senses.title: To put into bottles
senses.definition: to put a liquid into bottles for sale
senses.definitionCN: 把液体装入瓶中以便出售
senses.example: The wine is bottled in France.
senses.exampleCN: 这种葡萄酒在法国装瓶。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for filling the container.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，表示把东西装进容器。

intro.en: Bottle goes back to a Latin word for a cask.
intro.cn: bottle 可上溯到拉丁语中表示木桶的词。

items.en: buttis meant a cask or a barrel.
items.cn: buttis 指木桶。

items.en: boteille meant a bottle.
items.cn: boteille 指瓶子。

items.en: botel named a glass container.
items.cn: botel 指玻璃容器。

items.en: bottling became an industry.
items.cn: 装瓶成为一项产业。

items.en: bottle covers the container, its amount and filling it.
items.cn: 如今 bottle 兼指瓶子、一瓶的量与装瓶。

note.en: The look-alike group rhymes with bottle; the near-meaning group names other containers.
note.cn: 形近组与 bottle 押韵；近义组是其他容器。

entries.definition: a small bottle for carrying liquid
a wide container with a lid

normalIntro.en: Bottle is a narrow neck over a round body, made to hold liquid.
normalIntro.cn: bottle 是细颈配圆身，专门用来装液体。

normal.en: Bottle and bottles are singular and plural.
normal.cn: 单数是 bottle，复数是 bottles。

normal.en: A bottle of water is a common phrase.
normal.cn: a bottle of water 是常见说法。

normal.en: Bottle up means to hold feelings inside.
normal.cn: bottle up 意为把情绪憋在心里。

normal.en: A bottle opener lifts the cap.
normal.cn: 开瓶器用来撬开瓶盖。

normal.en: Bottleneck means a narrow point that slows things.
normal.cn: bottleneck 指让事情变慢的瓶颈。

abstract.en: See an empty bottle on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上立着一只空瓶。

abstract.en: See wine poured into a glass bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象葡萄酒被灌进玻璃瓶。

abstract.en: See a narrow road with cars packed together.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄路上车挤成一团。

examples.en: An empty glass bottle stood on the table.
examples.cn: 桌上放着一只空玻璃瓶。

examples.en: He drank a whole bottle of water.
examples.cn: 他喝了一整瓶水。

examples.en: The wine is bottled in France.
examples.cn: 这种葡萄酒在法国装瓶。

dict_mnemonic.text: bottle 里的 t 像细长的瓶颈，两个 t 并排，正是瓶子收窄的地方。

root: bottle 源自拉丁语 buttis（木桶），经古法语 boteille 进入英语，先指玻璃容器，后引申为一瓶的量与装瓶的动作。

sensesIntro.en: A narrow-necked container, the liquid it holds, and the act of filling it.
sensesIntro.cn: 细颈容器、它盛装的液量，以及装瓶的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty glass bottle on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上立着的一只空玻璃瓶。

intro.en: Bottle takes -er and joins neck to make new words.
intro.cn: bottle 加 -er，并与 neck 组合成新词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin; the items below share the idea of holding liquid.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自拉丁语，下面的词都围绕盛装液体。

items.meaning: a narrow point that slows things
a wide container with a lid
